verses.54:3: {sum3a} no meu {exercitatio}: * e {sum3b} pela voz do inimigo, e pela tribulação do pecador.

verses.54:5: O meu coração {sum5} em mim: * e o pavor da morte caiu sobre mim.

verses.54:7: E eu disse: Quem me dará asas como as da pomba, * {volabo}?
verses.54:9: Eu aguardava aquele que me salvou * do {pusill} e da tempestade.

verses.54:12: E não {defecit} das praças dela * a usura, e o engano.
verses.54:13: Porque, se o meu inimigo {maledixisset}, * eu o teria suportado, certamente.
verses.54:13b: E se aquele que me odiava tivesse falado grandezas contra mim, * talvez eu me tivesse escondido dele.

verses.54:24b: Os homens de sangue e enganadores não {dimidiabunt}: * mas eu esperarei em vós, Senhor.

decisions.why: Ps 53:4 has the same words in another order (Deus, exáudi oratiónem meam → 'Deus, escutai a minha oração'). Identical words get identical Portuguese (rule 6): escutai (D3), the bare vocative Deus (Ps 53's decision `deus`), a minha oração. The order follows each Latin line, since both orders are natural Portuguese; so a reader crossing columns finds the vocative where the Latin puts it.

options.label: Escutai, Deus,
options.note: Draft. The Latin's order; 53:4's words.

options.label: Deus, escutai
options.note: 53:4's order, so that the two psalms open alike to the ear. The Latin does not open them alike.

options.label: Escutai, ó Deus,
options.note: MS1932 ('Ouve, ó Deus'). The interjection is not in the Latin; Ps 53 refused it.

decisions.why: despícere with God as subject → desdenhar (glossary, open: 9:22, 21:25 'nem desdenhou a prece do pobre', 26:9b 'nem me desdenheis'). 21:25 has the same object, deprecátio → prece (D35). The blind reader of Ps 9 did not know 'desdenhais' but heard 'despises'.

options.label: desdenheis
options.note: Draft; the glossary row as applied in 21:25 and 26:9b.

options.label: desprezeis
options.note: MS1932 'não desprezes'; the plainer word, but 21:25 keeps desprezar for spérnere beside it.

decisions.latin: Contristátus sum … conturbátus sum … Cor meum conturbátum est
decisions.why: Three perfect passives saying a state that holds now. Portuguese says the state with estar + participle ('estou perturbado'); the past tense ('entristeci-me') tells an event. Ps 6:3–4 said the same Latin as a state ('os meus ossos estão perturbados'). contristári → entristecer-se (D42), conturbáre → perturbar (glossary).

options.label: Estou entristecido … estou perturbado … está perturbado
options.note: Draft; the state, as 6:3–4. MS1932 'Estou triste … estou conturbado … está perturbado'.

options.label: Entristeci-me … perturbei-me … se perturbou
options.note: The perfect as an event.

decisions.why: The only place of the noun. The verb exercéri stands seven times (76:4, 76:7, 76:13; 118:15, 23, 27, 48, 78) and Ps 118 renders it 'exercitar-se' ('Nos vossos mandamentos me exercitarei'); the Greek here is ἀδολεσχία, the noun of the verb behind 118:15 (musing, pondering). DRB 'I am grieved in my exercise'. The cognate keeps the family and the Latin word; the risk is that 'exercício' is heard as bodily exercise. MS1932's 'provação' explains, and says trial, which the Latin does not.

options.label: exercício
options.note: Draft. The Latin's word and Ps 118's family (exercitar-se); DRB 'exercise'.

options.label: meditação
options.note: The Greek's sense (ἀδολεσχία); but meditátio is another Latin word (1:2, 18:15, 118:97), and this would collide with it.

options.label: provação
options.note: MS1932. Explains; says trial.

decisions.why: The same build as 20:12 'declinavérunt in te mala' → 'voltaram males contra vós' (the stylist's verb, taken there). The Latin does not say whether iniquitátes is the subject (iniquities turned upon me) or the object (they turned iniquities upon me; the Greek has an object, ἐξέκλιναν … ἀνομίαν, and DRB 'they have cast iniquities upon me'). 'voltaram iniquidades contra mim' holds both readings, as 20:12 does.

options.label: voltaram iniquidades contra mim
options.note: Draft; 20:12's build. Subject or object left open.

options.label: lançaram iniquidades sobre mim
options.note: DRB 'cast'. Makes the enemies the subject and changes the verb.

options.label: desviaram iniquidades contra mim
options.note: Ps 20:12 draft 1 (declináre's own verb, 13:3a); refused there by the stylist.

decisions.why: contéxere is to weave together, to cover over (only here in the psalter, grep); the Greek ἐκάλυψεν is 'covered'. 'envolveram' keeps something of the Latin's wrapping; 'cobriram' is the Greek and 43:20's word for coopérire ('a sombra da morte nos cobriu').

options.label: envolveram
options.note: Draft; MS1932 'as trevas me envolveram'. Kept apart from coopérire → cobrir (43:20).

options.label: cobriram
options.note: The Greek; DRB 'covered'. Merges with coopérire.

decisions.why: The Latin coordinates two futures after the wish 'Quis dabit mihi…?' (DRB 'and I will fly and be at rest?'). MS1932 turns them into purpose ('para voar e descansar'), which is how Portuguese usually builds it. The coordination is kept: it is sayable and the question still carries it. requiéscere → repousar (glossary).

options.label: e voarei, e repousarei
options.note: Draft; the Latin's futures and double 'et'.

options.label: para voar e repousar
options.note: MS1932's build; purpose where the Latin coordinates.

decisions.why: elongáre keeps the Latin's 'longe' in this project (glossary, open: 21:20, 39:12 'pôr longe'); here it is intransitive, 'I went far off' (ἐμάκρυνα). 'afastar-se' is discédere's (glossary). The participle fúgiens stays a participle.

options.label: Eis que fui para longe, fugindo

forms.elongavi: Eis que fui para longe, fugindo

options.note: Draft; the 'longe' of the row; DRB 'I have gone far off flying away'.

options.label: Eis que me afastei fugindo
options.note: MS1932. afastar is discédere's.

decisions.why: solitúdo is a lonely place, a wilderness (ἐρήμῳ), and also loneliness. Portuguese 'solidão' has both senses too, the second first. 'deserto' is the Greek and DRB's 'wilderness', MS1932's 'deserto', but it spends desértum's word (28:8, 77:40, 105:14 …). 101:7 'pellicáno solitúdinis' and 106:4 'Erravérunt in solitúdine' will test the row.

options.label: solidão
options.note: Draft; the Latin's word with its two senses.

options.label: deserto
options.note: MS1932; the place only; desértum's word.

decisions.why: pusillanímitas (only here, grep) is smallness of soul, faint-heartedness (ὀλιγοψυχία). The cognate 'pusilanimidade' is a real word but six syllables and bookish; 'desânimo' says lack of heart plainly; MS1932 'abatimento' says dejection.

options.label: desânimo de espírito
options.note: Draft; the plainer of two faithful words (D2).

options.label: pusilanimidade de espírito
options.note: The cognate; DRB 'pusillanimity of spirit'. Long and learned.

decisions.why: The Latin imperative has no object of its own (καταπόντισον, 'sink them'). Bare 'Precipitai, Senhor' is heard in Portuguese as 'hasten, Lord' — a wrong first hearing. The object 'them' (the enemies of the next colon) is supplied, as MS1932 does ('Precipita-os'); DRB 'Cast down, O Lord'.

options.label: Precipitai-os
options.note: Draft; the object supplied, as MS1932.

options.label: Precipitai
options.note: The Latin's bare verb; heard as 'hasten'.

decisions.why: The bare 'dividi as suas línguas' is banned (rule 3: 'dividi' is also 'I divided'). D13 lets the imperative stand with an enclitic pronoun: 'dividi-lhes as línguas'. Here the ear is helped further by the imperative 'Precipitai-os' and the vocative 'Senhor' just before it in the same colon. dividere comes back at 54:21 'divísi sunt' → 'foram divididos', so the psalm's one verb is kept. 'fendei' (split) avoids the question but loses that echo; MS1932 'confunde' says Babel, not the Latin.

options.label: dividi-lhes as línguas
options.note: Draft; D13's enclitic imperative; the echo with 54:21 kept.

options.label: fendei as suas línguas
options.note: Safe at the vós imperative (fendei ≠ fendi); another verb from 54:21.

options.label: dividi as suas línguas
options.note: The bare form; banned by rule 3. For reference only.

decisions.why: contradíctio → contenda (glossary, open: 17:44, 30:21b; ἀντιλογία). 54:10 is one of the places the row lists. The blind reader of Ps 17 heard 'contradições' as inconsistencies.

options.label: contenda
options.note: Draft; the row.

options.label: contradição
options.note: MS1932, DRB; the cognate.

decisions.latin: Et non defécit de platéis ejus
decisions.why: defícere de: 'has not failed from, not gone out of' her streets (οὐκ ἐξέλιπεν ἐκ). The glossary's 'desfalecer' is for defícere of strength and soul; with 'de' and a place it is 'go missing from'. The Latin verb is singular with two subjects; Portuguese makes it plural (grammar).

options.label: desapareceram
options.note: Draft; 'failed from' as 'gone missing from'.

options.label: se afastaram
options.note: MS1932. afastar-se is discédere's.

options.label: faltaram
options.note: Literal 'failed'; 'faltar de' is awkward.

decisions.why: maledícere is to curse or revile (the Greek ὠνείδισεν is 'reproached'; DRB 'reviled'). Proposed row: maledícere → amaldiçoar, against benedícere → bendizer (D11); 108:28 'Maledícent illi, et tu benedíces' will test whether the pair must become 'maldizer … bendizer'.

options.label: me tivesse amaldiçoado
options.note: Draft; the Latin's word.

options.label: tivesse falado mal de mim
options.note: MS1932; 'speak ill', the root's parts.

options.label: me tivesse insultado
options.note: The Greek's sense (ὠνείδισεν); obloqui → insultar (D43) already has it.

decisions.latin: Tu vero, homo … / Tu vero, Deus …
decisions.why: The Latin turns twice with the same words: to the false friend (54:14) and to God (54:24). Rule 3 splits the pronoun (a singular man is tu, God is vós), so the echo can only be kept in the rest of the phrase: '… porém' in both. 'Vós, porém, Senhor' is 40:11's Tu autem.

options.label: Tu, porém / Vós, porém
options.note: Draft; the two turns sound alike but for the pronoun; 40:11's build.

options.label: Mas tu / Mas vós
options.note: MS1932's 'Mas tu'; 'mas' is also the psalm's ego autem at 54:24b, so two 'mas' back to back at the close.

decisions.why: unánimis, 'of one soul' (ἰσόψυχε, 'equal-souled'), of one man: of one mind with me. Portuguese 'unânime' is said of groups. 'de uma só alma' keeps both parts of the Latin word; whether 'with me' is heard is left to the verse's second colon and to 54:15 'comigo', as in the Latin. MS1932 'que eras um comigo' explains.

options.label: de uma só alma
options.note: Draft; úna ánima.

options.label: de uma só alma comigo
options.note: 'with me' supplied; closes the reading 'single-souled'. Repeats 'comigo' of 54:15.

options.label: unânime
options.note: The cognate; DRB 'a man of one mind'. Said of groups in Portuguese.

decisions.why: notus is 'one known to me', a familiar (γνωστέ). 30:12 'timor notis meis' → 'temor para os meus conhecidos', and 87:9, 87:19 have the plural. 'conhecido' in Brazil can sound like a mere acquaintance, which undercuts a lament about a close friend; but the Latin word is that word, and the verse says the closeness itself (unánimis, dux).

options.label: conhecido
options.note: Draft; 30:12's word.

options.label: íntimo
options.note: DRB 'my familiar'; says the closeness; a proparoxytone at the final.

options.label: amigo
options.note: MS1932. Another word (amícus, 87:19).

decisions.why: The relative runs on from 54:14's vocative. 'Que' at the head of a verse can be heard as an exclamation; 'Tu que' names the subject again. Draft keeps the Latin's bare relative after the colon that ends 54:14.

options.label: Que juntamente
options.note: Draft; MS1932 'que tomavas juntamente comigo'.

options.label: Tu que juntamente
options.note: The subject named (D2).

decisions.why: cibus → food (glossary esca / cibus, open); with dulces, 'sweet foods'. 'manjar' is a dish, a delicacy — current and not archaic; 'alimentos' is flat and clinical beside 'doces'. dulcis → doce (glossary).

options.label: doces manjares
options.note: Draft; MS1932 'doces manjares'.

options.label: doces alimentos
options.note: The plainer noun.

decisions.why: ambulávimus is perfect, but in Portuguese 'andamos' is both present and preterite, and the present ('we walk') would say the friendship still stands, which is the opposite of the verse. The imperfect 'andávamos' matches 'tomavas' (capiébas) and says it was so and is no more. Tense is grammar (D2).

options.label: andávamos
options.note: Draft; MS1932.

options.label: andamos
options.note: The Latin's perfect; heard as present.

decisions.why: consénsus (only here) is agreement, concord (ἐν ὁμονοίᾳ, 'in one-mindedness'). 'com consenso' is a committee's word. 'em concórdia' is the plain Portuguese for walking together in agreement.

options.label: em concórdia
options.note: Draft.

options.label: de comum acordo
options.note: Heard as 'by mutual decision'.

options.label: com consenso
options.note: The cognate; DRB 'with consent'.

decisions.why: inférnus → inferno (glossary, open: 6:6, 17:6, 29:4, 30:18 'sejam conduzidos ao inferno'). Here the image is of the earth swallowing men alive (Num 16:33); 'desçam vivos ao inferno' is also MS1932's and DRB's ('go down alive into hell').

options.label: ao inferno
options.note: Draft; the row.

options.label: à mansão dos mortos
options.note: The row's option: the abode of the dead.

decisions.why: Obscure in the Latin, as in the Greek (ὅτι ἐν πολλοῖς ἦσαν σὺν ἐμοί): 'among many they were with me' — they were many with me (against me), or I was not alone. DRB keeps it word for word. MS1932 resolves it ('porque eles são muitos contra mim'), turning 'with' into 'against'.

options.label: porque entre muitos estavam comigo
options.note: Draft; the Latin's words, the ambiguity left.

options.label: porque eram muitos contra mim
options.note: MS1932's reading; resolves, and changes 'with' to 'against'.

decisions.why: The relative is God's, held back to the end of the verse. 'ele, que é antes dos séculos' names him again with the lightest word, so that the colon does not hang and is not heard as 'what is before the ages'; 'é' keeps est. MS1932 'aquele que existe antes dos séculos'; D39 keeps 'existir' for absolute esse, which this is not.

options.label: ele, que é antes dos séculos

forms.ante_saecula: ele, que é antes dos séculos

options.note: Draft (after checks: 'aquele que é' was +4 against the Latin's seven syllables).

options.label: aquele que é antes dos séculos

forms.ante_saecula: aquele que é antes dos séculos

options.note: First pencilled form; +4.

options.label: aquele que existe antes dos séculos

forms.ante_saecula: aquele que existe antes dos séculos

decisions.why: commutátio → troca is settled (D43) for 43:13, where it is a sale ('nas trocas deles'); D43 says 88:52 decides its own sense, and so must this verse. Here the Latin is read by both Vulgate-family witnesses as change (DRB 'there is no change with them', MS1932 'não há mudança neles'): they do not change, and do not fear God. The Greek ἀντάλλαγμα is 'something given in exchange' (a ransom), so 'troca' keeps the Greek, and 'mudança' the Latin as it was read. 'para eles' keeps the dative's openness ('they have no change' / 'there is none for them').

options.label: mudança
options.note: Draft; DRB, MS1932; the local sense D43 allows.

options.label: troca
options.note: D43's word; the Greek's 'exchange'. Heard as a swap.

decisions.why: in + gerund: 'in repaying'. Portuguese has no 'em retribuir'; 'para retribuir' makes it purpose (DRB 'to repay'), 'ao retribuir' makes it time. Who stretches out the hand — God or the traitor — the Latin leaves open, and so does 'estendeu a sua mão'. retribúere → retribuir (glossary).

options.label: para retribuir
options.note: Draft; DRB.

options.label: ao retribuir
options.note: 'when repaying'.

decisions.why: contamináre (here and 105:39 'contamináta est in opéribus eórum') is to defile, pollute (ἐβεβήλωσαν, 'profaned'). The cognate is current and keeps the image of stain; 'profanar' (MS1932) is the Greek's word. testaméntum → aliança (glossary).

options.label: Contaminaram
options.note: Draft; the Latin's word, as 105:39 will want.

options.label: Profanaram
options.note: MS1932; the Greek.

decisions.latin: Mollíti sunt sermónes ejus super óleum
decisions.why: 'His words were made soft beyond oil.' The verb is kept as a becoming ('tornaram-se mais brandas'); MS1932 'são mais suaves que o azeite' drops it. sermo → palavra (D15). oleum → óleo, as 22:5b and 44:8 have it ('azeite' is 4:8's oil as produce).

options.label: As suas palavras tornaram-se mais brandas que o óleo

forms.molliti: As suas palavras tornaram-se mais brandas que o óleo

options.note: Draft.

options.label: As suas palavras amoleceram mais que o óleo

forms.molliti: As suas palavras amoleceram mais que o óleo

options.note: The verb itself; 'amolecer' says soft, not smooth.

options.label: As suas palavras são mais suaves que o azeite

forms.molliti: As suas palavras são mais suaves que o azeite

options.note: MS1932; the verb dropped.

decisions.why: Spoken to a single hearer: tu (rule 3). cura is care, anxiety (μέριμνα). 'o teu cuidado' is the Latin's number and word; MS1932 has the plural 'os teus cuidados', which is how the phrase is often said.

options.label: o teu cuidado
options.note: Draft; DRB 'thy care'.

options.label: os teus cuidados
options.note: MS1932; the plural.

options.label: a tua preocupação
options.note: The plainest modern word for the anxiety; flatter.

decisions.latin: non dabit in ætérnum fluctuatiónem justo
decisions.why: 'He will not give wavering to the just for ever' (οὐ δώσει … σάλον, a tossing like the sea's). L&S: fluctuátio, 'wavering, vacillation'. dare + noun is an idiom for 'allow'; Portuguese says it with 'deixar' + infinitive (the glossary's 'dare + inf. → deixar + inf.'). 'para sempre não …' is the build of 14:5b and 29:7 ('para sempre não será abalado'). The noun is made a verb: grammar, not sense.

options.label: para sempre não deixará vacilar o justo

forms.fluctuatio: para sempre não deixará vacilar o justo

options.note: Draft; ends on the Latin's last word.

options.label: não dará para sempre agitação ao justo

forms.fluctuatio: não dará para sempre agitação ao justo

options.note: dare and the noun kept; MS1932's 'agitação'.

decisions.why: D22's 'guiar' is for guidance (deduc me). When dedúcere takes men or things down to a place below, the psalms so far said 'fazer descer' (7:6 'faça descer ao pó', 21:16 'me fizestes descer ao pó da morte'); 30:18 'deducántur in inférnum' has 'sejam conduzidos'. The Greek here is κατάξεις, 'bring down'. intéritus → destruição (glossary).

options.label: fareis descer
options.note: Draft; 7:6, 21:16; DRB 'bring them down'.

options.label: conduzireis
options.note: MS1932; 30:18's verb. Safe outside the imperative.

decisions.why: dimidiáre (only here) is to halve: 'they will not halve their days', i.e. not live half of them (ἡμισεύσωσιν). The word for word 'não dividirão ao meio os seus dias' is not understood. MS1932 'não chegarão à metade dos seus dias' keeps the half and says it plainly.

options.label: chegarão à metade dos seus dias

forms.dimidiabunt: chegarão à metade dos seus dias

options.note: Draft; MS1932.

options.label: viverão a metade dos seus dias

forms.dimidiabunt: viverão a metade dos seus dias

options.note: DRB 'shall not live out half their days'.

choices.54:2: D3 escutar (twice, the Latin's repetition kept) and atender for inténde; 'atendei-me' has a pronoun object, so D40's 'atender em' does not arise. deprecátio → prece (D35).
choices.54:3: a voce … a tribulatióne: 'pela' for the cause, twice, as the Latin repeats 'a'. tribulátio → tribulação; peccátor → pecador.
choices.54:4: molésti esse → importunar, as the glossary row directs (34:13; this is the only other place). The Greek here is ἐνεκότουν ('bore a grudge'), not 34:13's παρενοχλεῖν; the Latin word is one, so the Portuguese is one. in ira → 'com ira' (the Latin has no possessive).
choices.54:5: in me → 'em mim', as 41:5; formído → pavor (the noun of the formidáre row).
choices.54:6: timor … tremor → temor … tremor (glossary; the Latin's own chime).
choices.54:7: pennæ → asas (glossary, open; no alæ in this psalm to collide with). sicut colúmbæ → 'como as da pomba'. Quis dabit → 'Quem … dará' (13:7).
choices.54:9: exspectáre → aguardar (D24), imperfect as 118:166 'Eu aguardava'. salvum me fecit → 'me salvou' (17:20). tempéstas → tempestade.
choices.54:11: circumdáre → cercar (glossary); the city (eam, ejus) is 'dela' in both colons and in 54:12, so that 'os seus muros' is not heard as the iniquity's. labor → fadiga (glossary); injustítia → injustiça. 'há' supplied in the verbless second colon (D2). die ac nocte → 'de dia e de noite' (31:4, 41:4).
choices.54:13: sustinére of a thing endured → suportar (glossary row sustinére). útique → certamente, at the end as in the Latin — which also breaks the rhyme 'amaldiçoado / suportado' that checks flagged at mediant and final. The second colon stays +5: one Latin word (sustinuíssem) needs four. The two conditions of 54:13 and 54:13b are built alike.
choices.54:13b: magna loqui super me → falar grandezas contra mim (D39, as 37:17). fórsitan → talvez. The long first colon (+4 against the Latin) comes from Portuguese's compound pluperfect; no word is supplied.
choices.54:14: A singular human addressee: tu (rule 3), the false friend. dux → guia (ἡγεμών). The vocative drops the article before the possessives ('meu guia'), as vocatives do.
choices.54:16b: nequítia → maldade (glossary), plural as the Latin; 'há' supplied. habitáculum → morada (32:14). eórum … eórum → 'deles … deles': the Latin's echo kept.
choices.54:17: ego autem → 'eu, porém' here and 'mas eu' at 54:24b (the glossary row allows both). 'Mas eu clamei a Deus' was four syllables short of the Latin colon; 'Eu, porém' also answers 54:14's 'Tu, porém': the Latin's turn from the false friend to God and back.
choices.54:18: narráre → narrar; annuntiáre → anunciar (D41). 'ele' supplied as subject of exáudiet. véspere → 'de tarde', the hour of Vespers.
choices.54:19: redímere → resgatar (glossary); appropinquáre → aproximar-se (glossary), echoed at 54:21 'se aproximou'.
choices.54:21: divísi sunt → 'foram divididos', the verb of 54:10 (dividi-lhes). ab ira vultus ejus → 'pela ira do seu rosto'; vultus → rosto. The Latin changes the pronoun (ejus … illíus); 'seu … dele' follows it without deciding who is meant.
choices.54:22: ipsi (the words) → 'elas mesmas'. jácula → dardos (MS1932); sagítta → seta stays apart.
choices.54:23: The second singular addressee (Jacta … te): tu (rule 3). enutríre → nutrir (glossary, 30:4). in ætérnum → para sempre (D23).
choices.54:24: God is vós; the echo with 54:14 is kept in 'porém' (decision `tuvero`). púteus → poço; intéritus → destruição (glossary).
choices.54:24b: viri sánguinum et dolósi → 'os homens de sangue e enganadores', as the glossary row foresaw (D29; dolósus → enganador). ego autem → 'mas eu'; speráre in → esperar em (D36).

Hard pass. Fixed after the first run: a doubled comma in the `tuvero` forms; 54:13 rhyme (amaldiçoado / suportado) broken by the Latin's order (suportado, certamente); 54:17a −4 (Mas eu → Eu, porém; now −3); 54:20 second colon +4 (aquele que é → ele, que é; now +3). Accepted: 54:20a −3 (humiliábit is long); 54:2a −6 (the Latin's long compounds); 54:10b −4 (contradictiónem, civitáte); 54:16b a −4; 54:5a +3, 54:11a +3, 54:12b +3, 54:13b a +4, 54:15a +3, 54:18a +3, 54:21a +3, 54:22a +4, 54:24b a +4 (articles, compound tenses, Portuguese's longer words; none adds a word the Latin lacks beyond supplied copulas). Rhymes accepted because the Latin has the same echo: 54:5 mim / mim (in me / super me), 54:16b deles / deles (eórum / eórum), 54:9 / 54:10 tempestade / cidade (tempestáte / civitáte). Oxytone cadences where the Latin is paroxytone (mim, pecador, salvou, solidão, voz, Senhor …) are allowed by rule 4.
